newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures higher on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures higher on weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended higher across the board on Wednesday, lifted by the yen's weakness against the dollar and firmer spot prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to 13 yen per gram higher, with benchmark August up 12 yen at 1,344.
Platinum futures ranged from 10 yen to 18 yen per gram higher. Benchmark August was 17 yen up at 1,366 yen.
In the platinum market, short-covering by overseas funds was noted during Asian hours, while Japanese trade houses sold spot platinum while buying futures in arbitrage.

"Overseas funds covered their shorts, supported by news that the U.S. government will go ahead with plans to issue platinum coins next year," one trader said, adding they had been waiting for the timing for covering shorts.
Spot platinum was quoted at $383.00/75 per ounce at the Tokyo close.
In the gold and platinum futures market, private investors were liquidating their long positions.
Despite of the yen's weaker tendency, investors' interest in precious metals futures remained weak amid a lack of buying incentives, the traders said.
Spot was quoted at $378.55/378.85 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $378.70/379.20 in New York on Tuesday.
The dollar advanced further against the yen on Wednesday, hitting a 33-month high of 111.92 yen.
Silver and palladium futures also ended firmer on the heels on gold, in activity mainly dominated by position-adjustment trade.
Silver futures ranged from 1.0 yen to 2.4 yen per 10 grams firmer, with benchmark August ending 1.8 yen up at 177.7 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from two to nine yen per gram higher. Benchmark August was five yen firmer at 427 yen.
